     2	# karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh — Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes),
     3	# per-task diff size (#961 K-1 / FR-1; reworked by cycle-129 D-4.3, D-4.2a,
     4	# DEC-0141).
     5	#
     6	# PostToolUse:Write|Edit|NotebookEdit hook. Counts the lines each write adds
     7	# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string) and keeps a running total
     8	# PER TASK:
     9	#
    10	#   key      the current task from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`
    11	#            (`.checkpoint.task`, else the sprint), else the session id from
    12	#            the hook payload (`.session_id`, else LOA_SESSION_ID, else
    13	#            <user>-<UTC date>); sanitised to ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (any other
    14	#            byte becomes `_`, a leading dot becomes `_`, cut to 128 bytes)
    15	#   state    .run/karpathy-surgical/<key>.jsonl — one small file per task, so
    16	#            the total resets when the task changes; the directory keeps the
    17	#            20 most recently written files and deletes older ones
    18	#   summary  .run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json
    19	#            {task, lines, threshold, over, updated_at}, rewritten atomically
    20	#            after each counted write; the review's SURGICAL axis reads it
    21	#   legacy   .run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl (the old session-long total) and
    22	#            its two perf caches are deleted on the first run of this layout
    23	#
    24	# Over `karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task` (default 100) it prints the
    25	# `[karpathy-surgical-warn]` stderr line and appends a trajectory event
    26	# (karpathy-check.payload.schema.json). Non-blocking: always exits 0. The
    27	# master switch `karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning` is read through
    28	# loa_knob (explicit key, else the loa.profile default; `lean` turns it off).
    29	#
    30	# Safety (NFR-Sec-1): tool_input.content / new_string never reach state,
    31	# summary or trajectory — only line counts, the file path (JSON-encoded by
    32	# jq) and the sanitised key. Missing jq or yq, a missing config or a
    33	# malformed payload is a silent no-op. A symlinked state directory or state
    34	# file is not written through.
    35	#
    36	# Seams (tests): LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (config), KARPATHY_STATE_DIR,
    37	# KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE, KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE, KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR,
    38	# KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD (default .claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh, which
    39	# itself honours LOA_RUN_DIR), KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP (default 20).
    40	#
    41	# Design note: the session-long state file grew without bound, which is what
    42	# the earlier perf passes (config-token and state-aggregate caches) existed
    43	# to absorb. Per-task files are small and rotated, so the hook reads them in
    44	# full each time and those caches are gone.
    45	
    46	set -uo pipefail
    47	umask 077
    48	export LC_ALL=C
    49	
    50	_src="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
    51	_src_dir="${_src%/*}"
    52	[[ "$_src_dir" == "$_src" ]] && _src_dir="."
    53	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$_src_dir" && pwd)"
    54	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
    55	DEFAULT_CONFIG="$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml"
    56	CONFIG="${LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE:-$DEFAULT_CONFIG}"
    57	DEFAULT_STATE_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical"
    58	STATE_DIR="${KARPATHY_STATE_DIR:-$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR}"
    59	SUMMARY="${KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-surgical-summary.json}"
    60	LEGACY="${KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE:-$REPO_ROOT/.run/karpathy-task-state.jsonl}"
    61	TRAJ_DIR="${KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory}"
    62	CHECKPOINT="${KARPATHY_CHECKPOINT_CMD:-$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh}"
    63	KEEP="${KARPATHY_STATE_KEEP:-20}"
    64	[[ "$KEEP" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ && "$KEEP" -ge 1 ]] || KEEP=20
    65	
    66	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
    67	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
    68	[[ -f "$CONFIG" ]] || exit 0
    69	
    70	# --- master switch and threshold (loa_knob: explicit key > profile > fallback)
    71	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh
    72	source "$REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
    73	if [[ "$CONFIG" != "$DEFAULT_CONFIG" ]]; then export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG"; fi
    74	switch="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true 2>/dev/null)"
    75	case "$switch" in
    76	    false|False|FALSE|0|no|No|NO|off|Off|OFF) exit 0 ;;
    77	esac
    78	THRESHOLD="$(loa_knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100 2>/dev/null)"
    79	[[ "$THRESHOLD" =~ ^[0-9]{1,9}$ ]] || THRESHOLD=100
    80	THRESHOLD=$((10#$THRESHOLD))
    81	
    82	# --- payload: one jq, one JSON-encoded field per line (no raw newlines) ---
    83	payload="$(cat)"
    84	[[ -n "$payload" ]] || exit 0
    85	fields="$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '
    86	    def slines: if . == "" then 1 else (split("\n") | length) end;
    87	    def jl: if type == "array" or type == "object"
    88	            then (if length == 0 then 1 else 2 + ([.[] | jl] | add) end)
    89	            else 1 end;
    90	    def count: if . == null or . == false then 0 elif type == "string" then slines else jl end;
    91	    select(type == "object") |
    92	    (.tool_name // "" | if type == "string" then . else tojson end) as $tn |
    93	    ([($tn | tojson),
    94	      (if $tn == "Write" then (.tool_input.content | count)
    95	       elif ($tn == "Edit" or $tn == "NotebookEdit") then (.tool_input.new_string | count)
    96	       else 0 end | tostring),
    97	      ((.tool_input.file_path // "<unknown>") | (if type == "string" then . else tojson end) | tojson),
    98	      ((.session_id // "") | (if type == "string" then . else "" end) | tojson),
    99	      (now | todate)] | .[])
   100	' 2>/dev/null | head -5)" || exit 0
   101	{
   102	    IFS= read -r TOOL_JSON
   103	    IFS= read -r LINES
   104	    IFS= read -r FILE_JSON
   105	    IFS= read -r PAYLOAD_SID_JSON
   106	    IFS= read -r TS
   107	} <<< "$fields"
   108	case "${TOOL_JSON:-}" in
   109	    '"Write"') TOOL_NAME=Write ;;
   110	    '"Edit"') TOOL_NAME=Edit ;;
   111	    '"NotebookEdit"') TOOL_NAME=NotebookEdit ;;
   112	    *) exit 0 ;;
   113	esac
   114	[[ "${LINES:-}" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ ]] || exit 0
   115	[[ -n "${FILE_JSON:-}" && -n "${TS:-}" ]] || exit 0
   116	
   117	# --- the key ------------------------------------------------------------------
   118	_sanitise() {  # stdin-free: $1 → ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (may print empty)
   119	    local s
   120	    s="$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_' | cut -c1-128)"
   121	    [[ "$s" == .* ]] && s="_${s#.}"
   122	    printf '%s' "$s"
   123	}
   124	payload_sid="$(printf '%s' "${PAYLOAD_SID_JSON:-\"\"}" | jq -r '.' 2>/dev/null)" || payload_sid=""
   125	SESSION="${payload_sid:-${LOA_SESSION_ID:-}}"
   126	[[ -n "$SESSION" ]] || SESSION="${USER:-unknown}-${TS:0:4}${TS:5:2}${TS:8:2}"
   127	SESSION_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg s "$SESSION" '$s')"
   128	
   129	task_raw=""
   130	if [[ -f "$CHECKPOINT" ]]; then
   131	    task_raw="$(bash "$CHECKPOINT" read --json 2>/dev/null \
   132	        | jq -r '[.checkpoint.task?, .checkpoint.sprint?, .sprint?] | map(select(type == "string" and . != ""))
   133	                  | .[0] // empty | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._-]"; "_")' 2>/dev/null \
   134	        | head -1)" || task_raw=""
   135	fi
   136	KEY="$(_sanitise "$task_raw")"
   137	[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="$(_sanitise "$SESSION")"
   138	[[ -n "$KEY" ]] || KEY="session-unknown"
   139	
   140	# --- legacy layout: deleted on the first run under this one -------------------
   141	if [[ -e "$LEGACY" || -L "$LEGACY" ]]; then
   142	    rm -f -- "$LEGACY" 2>/dev/null || true
   143	    if [[ "$STATE_DIR" == "$DEFAULT_STATE_DIR" ]]; then
   144	        rm -f -- "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-state.v1.agg" \
   145	                 "$REPO_ROOT/.run/perf-cache/karpathy-config.v1.tokens" 2>/dev/null || true
   146	    fi
   147	fi
   148	
   149	# --- append to the task's file ------------------------------------------------
   150	[[ -L "$STATE_DIR" ]] && exit 0
   151	[[ -d "$STATE_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   152	TASK_FILE="$STATE_DIR/$KEY.jsonl"
   153	[[ -L "$TASK_FILE" ]] && exit 0
   154	
   155	PRIOR=0
   156	if [[ -f "$TASK_FILE" ]]; then
   157	    # Tolerant of malformed lines: sums every `"lines_changed":<int>` it finds.
   158	    PRIOR="$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '/"lines_changed":/ { sum += $2 + 0 } END { print sum + 0 }' "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null)" || PRIOR=0
   159	    [[ "$PRIOR" =~ ^[0-9]{1,15}$ ]] || PRIOR=0
   160	fi
   161	RUNNING=$((PRIOR + LINES))
   162	
   163	printf '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s,"task":"%s"}\n' \
   164	    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON" "$KEY" >> "$TASK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   165	
   166	# Keep the KEEP most recently written task files (names are sanitised: no
   167	# whitespace, no leading dot, so the glob and the ls listing are exact).
   168	n=0
   169	while IFS= read -r old; do
   170	    n=$((n + 1))
   171	    if (( n > KEEP )) && [[ "$old" != "$TASK_FILE" && ! -L "$old" ]]; then
   172	        rm -f -- "$old" 2>/dev/null || true
   173	    fi
   174	done < <(ls -1t -- "$STATE_DIR"/*.jsonl 2>/dev/null)
   175	
   176	# --- summary (atomic) ---------------------------------------------------------
   177	OVER=false
   178	(( RUNNING > THRESHOLD )) && OVER=true
   179	sum_dir="${SUMMARY%/*}"
   180	[[ "$sum_dir" == "$SUMMARY" ]] && sum_dir="."
   181	if [[ -d "$sum_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$sum_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
   182	    tmp="$SUMMARY.tmp.$$"
   183	    if printf '{"task":"%s","lines":%s,"threshold":%s,"over":%s,"updated_at":"%s"}\n' \
   184	            "$KEY" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$OVER" "$TS" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
   185	        mv -f -- "$tmp" "$SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   186	    else
   187	        rm -f -- "$tmp" 2>/dev/null
   188	    fi
   189	fi
   190	
   191	# --- warning + trajectory event -----------------------------------------------
   192	if [[ "$OVER" == "true" ]]; then
   193	    echo "[karpathy-surgical-warn] Session diff total ${RUNNING} lines exceeds threshold ${THRESHOLD}. Karpathy principle 3 (Surgical Changes): verify every changed line traces to the stated task. State: $TASK_FILE" >&2
   194	
   195	    counts="$(jq -nr --rawfile s "$TASK_FILE" '
   196	        ($s | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))) as $l |
   197	        (try ([$l[] | fromjson | .file // empty] | unique | length) catch 0) as $f |
   198	        "\($f) \($l | length)"' 2>/dev/null)" || counts="0 0"
   199	    FILES_MOD="${counts%% *}"; TOOL_CALLS="${counts##* }"
   200	    [[ "$FILES_MOD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || FILES_MOD=0
   201	    [[ "$TOOL_CALLS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || TOOL_CALLS=0
   202	    [[ -d "$TRAJ_DIR" ]] || mkdir -p "$TRAJ_DIR" 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   203	    printf '{"phase":"karpathy_check","principle":"surgical_changes","timestamp":"%s","files_modified":%s,"lines_total":%s,"threshold":%s,"verdict":"warn","tool_call_count":%s,"session_id":%s}\n' \
   204	        "$TS" "$FILES_MOD" "$RUNNING" "$THRESHOLD" "$TOOL_CALLS" "$SESSION_JSON" \
   205	        >> "$TRAJ_DIR/karpathy-${TS:0:10}.jsonl" 2>/dev/null || true
   206	fi
   207	
   208	exit 0

content.content:
LINES="${_kf[1]}"
    TS="${_kf[2]}"
    FILE_JSON="${_kf[3]}"
    SESSION_JSON="${_kf[4]}"
    FILES_MOD="${_kf[5]}"
    TOOL_CALLS="${_kf[6]}"
fi

[[ -n "$TOOL_NAME" ]] || exit 0

# Tool dispatch. Lines were computed for the matching shape inside jq
# (Write → content, Edit/NotebookEdit → new_string — conservative, counts
# new content only; the v1 simplification documented in SDD §0.3).
case "$TOOL_NAME" in
    Write|Edit|NotebookEdit)
        ;;
    *)
        # Unrecognized tool — no-op (defensive: settings.json matcher should
        # prevent this, but the hook stays safe even if matcher widens).
        exit 0
        ;;
esac

[[ "$LINES" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || exit 0

# perf pass-4: skip the dirname+mkdir spawns when the parent dir already
# exists (the steady state). The guard passing proves dirname's target
# exists (e.g. "a/b" being a dir ⇒ "a" exists), so mkdir -p would be a
# no-op; every other shape (no slash, trailing slash, missing parent) takes
# the old command unchanged.
if [[ "${TASK_STATE%/*}" == "$TASK_STATE" || ! -d "${TASK_STATE%/*}" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TASK_STATE")"
fi

# Running total: sum lines_changed across existing state entries + this call.
# Awk parse is intentionally tolerant of malformed lines (skips them).
# perf pass-7: FAST serves the cached total (== the full scan's printed
# value: cache writes require an exact-decimal 15-digit integer); DELTA
# re-runs THE SAME awk program on only the token+delta bytes, seeded with
# the cached total in BEGIN — same association order as the full scan.
if [[ "$_kp7_sum_mode" == "fast" ]]; then
    RUNNING="$_kp7_bsum"
elif [[ "$_kp7_sum_mode" == "delta" ]]; then
    RUNNING=$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' -v init="$_kp7_bsum" '
        BEGIN { sum = init + 0 }
        NR == 1 { next }
        /"lines_changed":/ {
            n = $2 + 0  # extract leading integer
            sum += n
        }
        END { print sum + 0 }
    ' <(tail -c +"$_kp7_tail_from" -- "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
else
    RUNNING=$(awk -F'"lines_changed":' '
        /"lines_changed":/ {
            n = $2 + 0  # extract leading integer
            sum += n
        }
        END { print sum + 0 }
    ' "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
fi
RUNNING=$((RUNNING + LINES))

# Append entry to state — printf-assembled from jq-pre-encoded pieces;
# byte-identical to the old jq -nc output (see header note).
# perf pass-7: the line is built in a variable first (printf -v cannot
# fail; identical bytes) so it can double as the cache's prefix-integrity
# token; the append keeps the old failure shape.
printf -v _kp7_entry '{"ts":"%s","tool":"%s","file":%s,"lines_changed":%s,"running_total":%s,"session_id":%s}' \
    "$TS" "$TOOL_NAME" "$FILE_JSON" "$LINES" "$RUNNING" "$SESSION_JSON"
printf '%s\n' "$_kp7_entry" >> "$TASK_STATE" 2>/dev/null || exit 0

# Threshold check.

+# _bdb_hd_header <line> — parse one header line. Sets _hd_ops (heredoc count,

+# The #1245 header grammar (byte-identical to _bdb_scrub_cat_heredoc's).
+_bdb_hd_plain_cat() {

+### implement-gate.sh (FR-7; modes since cycle-129 FR-4(a))
 
-**Type**: Command hook (ADVISORY: asks, never blocks). **Wired by default** in `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/hooks/settings.hooks.json` through `hook-guard.sh`, matcher `Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit`.
+**Type**: Command hook. -**Output** (Claude Code PreToolUse contract): allow is a silent exit 0 with empty stdout; ask is exit 0 with `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"…"}}`. A top-level `decision` field is never emitted.

+
+**Modes** (`implement_gate.mode` in `.loa.config.yaml`; `/loa` prints the effective mode through `implement-gate.sh --effective-mode`, so the status line and the hook share one parser). The position is the derived `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` (`run-checkpoint.sh derive`); it is *known* when the cache parses and its `derived_at` is within `run_mode.stale_hours` (12 h).
+
+| Mode | Unsanctioned App-Zone write | Audit row |
+|------|-----------------------------|-----------|
+| `ask` (default; also unset or an unknown value) | ask | `ask/ask` |
+| `telemetry` | allow silently | `telemetry/outside_run` |
+| `deny` | deny while the position is known; ask when it is unknown (missing, stale, never derived or unparseable) | `deny/deny`, `ask/unknown_position` |
+
+`implement_gate.claims: authoritative` is the tighten-only modifier: a model-authored non-implementation claim in `tool_input.active_skill` asks (or is denied where `deny` would deny anyway); an implementation claim never allows by itself; an absent claim falls through. The deny reason ends with the two remedies (run the write inside `/implement` or `/bug`, or set `implement_gate.mode: ask`).
+
+**Sanctions** (checked in the order run, marker, override; each allows with its own row): a derived RUNNING cache with a fresh `derived_at` (`allow/sanctioned_run`); a fresh `.run/implement-active.json` marker, written by `run-checkpoint.sh mark` at the start of `implementing-tasks` and `bug-triaging` and removed by `unmark` at their end (`allow/sanctioned_marker`; a stale marker logs `stale_marker` and does not sanction); `LOA_IMPLEMENT_GATE_OVERRIDE=1` (`allow/override`, logged only when nothing else sanctioned). The legacy state files below keep sanctioning as before. This repository stays on `ask` until the cycle's last commit (DEC-0168).
 
 **Path rule**: the path is `tool_input.file_path`, or `tool_input.notebook_path` for NotebookEdit. A relative path resolves from the payload's `cwd`. content.text:
This PR should not merge. The review is in `/workspace/review.md`: 12 findings, verdict **CHANGES_REQUIRED**.

**Blocking:**

1. **The new heredoc classifier lets through commands the old fence blocked.** It's described as fail-closed, but I ran the old and new versions of `block-destructive-bash.sh` on the same commands. All three of these were blocked before and are allowed now:
   - **Reading the file into a shell:** `cat > n.txt <<'EOF' … then rm -rf ~ … EOF` followed by `cat n.txt | sh`. `cat` counts as a safe reader, and the check never links `| sh` back to the written file. The body scan also misses `rm` after shell keywords like `then`.
   - **Via git config:** a heredoc writes a git config file with an alias that runs `sh -c 'rm -rf ~'`, then `git -c include.path=<file> <alias>`. `git` is on the safe-reader list.
   - **Via files tools run on their own:** a `package.json` whose `postinstall` script is `rm -rf ~`, then `npm install`. The same gap covers Makefile/make and `.husky` hooks.
2. **Old review files halt runs.** The circuit-breaker recount treats any review file without the new verdict trailer as "changes required", even when the text approves. Those files also all hash the same. In a test fixture, three such "All good. Approved." rounds put the run into HALTED with the breaker open. That happens on every checkpoint write and every `mark`, and HALTED stays until someone resumes manually.
3. **`derive` breaks on jq 1.6.** It uses `$label` as a variable name, which jq 1.6 rejects (`label` is a keyword there). jq 1.6 is the default on Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 11; it's what this machine has, and I confirmed the failure here. With jq 1.7.1 it works. A rename fixes it.
4. **The retrospective scan turns on silently.** The `standard` profile sets `invisible_retrospective.enabled: true`. This repository's config doesn't set the key, and before this change the scan ran only on an explicit `true`. So this repo, and any install that omits the key, now runs it after every skill. The guardrail default changes got an explicit config block and a note; this one didn't.

**Lesser findings:**
- The surgical-diff hook's "per-task" counts get filed under the previous task, or under the whole sprint when `br` is unavailable. Every Write/Edit also now starts `run-checkpoint.sh` and `br show`.
- `/loa` prints two implement-gate lines that can contradict each other ("heuristic" next to "deny").
- `mark` can't replace a corrupted marker file.
- A breaker trip can return exit 3 instead of 10 when `state.json` can't be parsed, so run-mode doesn't halt.
- A stale marker writes two audit rows for one write, though the docs promise one.
- The lint self-test now accepts warnings on the clean fixture, so new warnings pass unnoticed.

**What I couldn't verify:** most of the PR's own bats suites fail in this checkout because the frozen tree lacks their fixtures, so I didn't use their results. My fixtures for findings 2 and 3 had no `verdict-derive.sh`, so I assumed it reports no trailer for an old-style file, which is what the script's fallback assumes.
